target.title: Gary Habermas - Chapter 002 - Powerful Historical Reasons to Believe Jesus Resurrected - Gary Habermas
target.domain: popular Christian apologetics lecture (auto-captioned YouTube transcript)
target.comparison_class: paper of similar purpose and evidence burden
target.population_boundary: speakers and named scholars/critics cited; no first-person affected parties beyond the lecturer and one emailer; report omissions
target.time_window: lecture undated; content covers 30 AD to present

gate_results.rationale: Historical claims are attributed to named scholars (Bart Ehrman, Dunn, Bauckham, Casey, Crossley) and texts (1 Cor 15:3ff, Gal 1-2), but citations are spoken, uncited by page, and several quantitative claims (100 evidences, 95%/75% consensus, 15 sources) are asserted without traceable sourcing.
gate_results.resolution: Would pass with page-level citations and consensus polling data.

gate_results.rationale: Internal tensions (Dunn vs Bauckham on the Shema; Habermas disagreeing with Ehrman on faith-as-evidence) are acknowledged and bounded, not concealed.
Historical method is used, then extended to 'that's the Christian worldview / that's the gospel' (S471-472) and to salvation as 'saying I do' (S682), which exceeds the historical method's domain.
Concedes 'history can't prove miracles' (S698) and names naturalistic alternatives, but does not state what evidence would defeat the six facts; the six are presented as beyond dispute.
Bridges history to theology/worldview (S466-472) without explicit bridge law or kill condition; the move is asserted rather than argued.
Named scholars and texts are traceable in principle, but auto-caption garbles names (Bartman/Bauckham, Fleiman/Philemon, Herertado/Hurtado) and no page or edition is given.
Persuasion by argument; the dissenting interlocutor (Crossley) is allowed to state his position and is not coerced; the angry atheist debate ends by the other party's choice.

contradictions.consequence: Dunn/Bauckham disagreement on the Shema is stated and answered, not hidden.
Habermas explicitly disagrees with Ehrman on faith-as-evidence; disagreement is bounded.
Consensus percentages (95%, 75%) and 'critics don't argue' are asserted without sourcing; if wrong, the minimal-facts argument weakens.

missing_evidence: Page-level citations for Bart Ehrman, Dunn, Bauckham, Casey, Crossley claims
Source of the '100 evidences' and '15 sources' counts
Speaker labels and clean names (auto-caption garbling)
Any affected-party or outsider review of the argument
repair_path: Cite page/edition for each attributed scholar claim
Give the polling or survey basis for consensus percentages
State what evidence would count against the six minimal facts
Separate historical conclusion from theological/worldview conclusion explicitly
falsifier: A documented, sourced survey showing that a substantial minority of critical scholars dispute one or more of the six minimal facts, or a citation showing a named scholar's position is misreported.
limitations: Auto-captioned transcript; names and numbers may be garbled.
Single lecture, not a full work; many claims are compressed.
No access to the underlying dissertation or book for verification.

Per-sentence summary supplied separately; I agree with its self_control negatives and its near-zero love/joy/peace/kindness/goodness means, and treat those as insufficient-evidence rather than anti-fruit.
